key_idea: In the 'beats' tournament graph a candidate can win under some agenda iff every other candidate is reachable from it along beats-edges.
sketch: Count pairwise preferences from the ballots (O(m n^2)) to get the tournament: i -> j if i beats j head to head. If x reaches everyone, order the agenda by decreasing BFS distance from x so each candidate is eventually knocked out by its BFS parent and x enters last; conversely any candidate that eliminated someone on the chain to the winner is reachable. Compute the transitive closure with Floyd-Warshall on at most 26 nodes and print 'can win' iff the row is all ones. Pitfalls: n = 1, and the output apostrophe is plain ASCII. Verified against trying all agendas for n <= 6.
